prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1261; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's representing attorney on the sideswipe that occurred while the claimant was changing lanes. The attorney advised that the claimant sustained a concussion and requested that all communication be routed through their office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver listed on the policy was the operator of the insured vehicle at the time of loss. Coverage was in force on the date of the incident and no issues with the policy have been identified.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle in the adjacent lane at the time of contact. Responding officers documented the lane change and the side contact between the two vehicles.

Entry 4: Statements from two independent witnesses match the claimant's account of the lane change and the contact that followed. Scene photographs were also reviewed and are consistent with that sequence of events.

Entry 5: Spoke with the other driver, whose account of the lane change and contact agrees with the claimant's version. No dispute has been raised regarding how the collision happened.

Entry 6: Inspected the insured vehicle and the damage to the rear quarter panel and mirror housing matches the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle has been found in the records or photographs reviewed.

Entry 7: Reviewed the claimant's medical file, which lists a concussion diagnosed after the collision. The reported symptoms are consistent with the type of injury expected from a crash of this kind.

Entry 8: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this diagnosis, and the treating provider has documented the ongoing course of care. No earlier injury to the same area of the head or neck appears in the medical history provided.

Entry 9: The claimant's representative provided a follow-up statement adding minor details about the seating position and the moment of impact. The core account has remained the same across all statements given to date.

Entry 10: Reviewed all information gathered to date. The claim is being handled on the basis of the consistent account, witness statements, physical evidence, and medical records, with the treatment timeline noted for ongoing review.
